This course aims to both teach C++ to people coming from Java and teach some fundamental data structures and algorithms that are used widely in computer science. While attempting to accomplish both of these goals, the course becomes unfocused and disorganized, which causes a majority of the students to lose interest in the course by the middle of the semester.

Let's start with the first goal of this course, teaching C++ to students coming from Java. C++ is a language with a very wide set of features and contains some concepts, like memory management, that are alien to people that only worked with languages like Java. Every CS student should definitely learn it, but the way CS201 attempts to teach it is flawed and very likely to cause problems while adapting to the real-world usage of the language. The course insists on using a very outdated C++ standard (C++03, which is basically C++98) for no good reason. The Standard Template Library--which contains implementations of every data structure taught in this course--already exists in C++98, and C++11 is widely supported by almost all recent compilers.  The course spends too much time on not-too-complex concepts like pointers, which leaves less time for actually teaching data structures. Since most of the C++ features are left unused, the course could use C instead, which is a simpler language that would require less time to teach, or it could demand knowledge about the basics of C++, which would give more time to actually teach data structures and algorithms, which is what the course is actually about! Most of my classmates learned C++ in their spare time or already knew the language before taking CS201, which made the first two-thirds of the course an even bigger waste of time. By the time this course actually became somewhat interesting, most people lost their interest in the course, which is a shame. 

The assignments also deserve a special mention, because whoever prepared them stopped caring a long time ago.
